newsitem.title: FINLAND: MERITA SEES VALUE IN FINNISH 2006 BOND AUCTION.
newsitem.headline: MERITA SEES VALUE IN FINNISH 2006 BOND AUCTION.

text.p: Merita Bank said it recommended participation in Thursday's auction of the serial 2006 bond to trading oriented accounts and said 3.5 billion markka of new liquidity due in coupon payments in mid-January is expected to support Finnish bonds.

"...3.5 billion (markka) of (1999 bond) coupon payments due in mid-January will support bonds as will the fact that the next bond auction will not be held until January 30," Merita research said in a pre-auction note dated January 8.
As the Finnish yield curve remains steep with the yield spread between the benchmark 2001 and 2006 bonds at 140 basis points, Merita said this would increase the attractiveness of the long end.
In the near-term, it said overseas markets were likely to be supportive of the Finnish bond market as the U.S. bond market seems to have reached a temporary in peak in yields.
"... with U.S. Treasuries discounting strong (December) payrolls number on Friday, a short-term bullish correction is possible," Merita said.
At 1200/1000 GMT, the 2006 bond yield was quoted at 6.34 percent, unchanged from Wednesday's close.
The auction results are due after 1330/1030 GMT. In the previous auction on November 21 the state treasury raised 1.12 billion markka at a yield of 6.45 percent.
